chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: The Kansas City house band and recycled show music
summary: A six-piece house band played their scores; music from shows such as Alabama School Days and a China scene was later reused, and no Kansas City musicians stand out.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How big a band was playing this music that you wrote? How many musicians?
About six pieces, but we didn't play it.

Yeah, they pretty good. They could read pretty good. They were all right, but that's all we had to db. He and I'd go down there to rehearsal the day that they rehearsed, and they would rehearse the songs and...and the choreographer would put on whatever they going to do--mostly walking, you know, and singing and going on, and we was through for the...until the next week. I mean, they'd give us the story for the next week, and we...and we uh...brought home all our music, and I think we had a lot of that old stuff. Like, we had "Alabama School Days." We had a school story one week. We wrote

all the music to "Alabama School Days," and we wrote...uh, a China scene. We wrote a lot of China music--my brother did--and I used that...got a job here for a picture a fellow made about China and used that China music. He called us to...I got a letter in there. I got a letter from him, and he...where he offered...he tried to get me to go to work in the...for the, uh...where you have the...where you have all the, uh, actors that go to get the jobs...broad...general... what is it?

Yeah! He wrote 'em a long letter to put me in there, you know, and if...uh, we wrote...he had a story that was Chinese, and we used all...a lot of our old Chinese music that we had in that show. Just looked it up, and went out there and we had fiddle--a couple of fiddles and a guitar, and I don't know what else--kinda represented Chinese band.
Do you remember any of the names of the musicians in Kansas City? Anybody stood out at all?
Mmmm mmmmm [no]. Only one I knew stood out was... I can't think of his name. He was a trumpet player...can't remember.
